trackPair.whatToListenFor: Young's music asks you to listen to one sound for a long time until you notice what is going on inside it. 'Discreet Music' asks the same thing, more gently: one soft phrase, repeating slowly, quiet enough to sit under a room. Listen for how long nothing seems to happen, and then notice how much has changed.

explanation: Brian Eno has called La Monte Young 'the daddy of us all', and has said that one of Young's early pieces was a cornerstone of everything he did after it. Both statements are Eno's own, reported with attribution in Wikipedia's article on Young. With Reich, this gives Eno's ambient work both of its minimalist parents: Young's long, unchanging sound and Reich's process that runs itself.
